text:
Sam L: Heads-up — we need to lock prioritization for pricing & packaging work this quarter. Reserved capacity vs usage-first model is the hot debate.
Anya K: +1. Can we table concrete criteria? impact, engineering effort, and enterprise demand are all pulling different directions.
Devon R: I ran a quick RICE on two options. Sharing calc.
pm-bot: 
```
RICE formula: R * I * C / Effort
Option A: ReservedCapacity (target enterprise deals)
Reach = 120 orgs/yr
Impact = 7 (revenue + adoption)
Confidence = 0.6
Effort = 8 dev-months
Score = (120*7*0.6)/8 = 63

Option B: TieredRateLimits + soft overage (target self-serve + growth)
Reach = 2,400 accounts/yr
Impact = 3
Confidence = 0.7
Effort = 5 dev-months
Score = (2400*3*0.7)/5 = 1008
```
Sam L: Interesting — RICE strongly favors tiered rate limits. But we shouldn't forget strategic value of ReservedCapacity (SLA, committed revenue).
Anya K: Exactly. RICE misses multi-quarter contract value and sales enablement. Can we add a scoring multiplier for strategic deals?
Max C: Technically, ReservedCapacity also requires infra changes (billing hooks, capacity reservation, quotas). I estimate ~8 dev-months + ops runway.
Priya S: From sales: 3 large prospects said they won't move to Dedicated without a formal reserved offering or contractual throughput guarantees. That's >$1M ARR opportunity each.
Devon R: Agree on urgency for a small, MVP reserved product — but we can sequence: do TieredRateLimits first to improve self-serve monetization, then ship a compact ReservedCapacity MVP for top enterprise deals.
Sam L: Proposed sequencing: 1) TieredRateLimits (fast, high reach), 2) ReservedCapacity MVP (sales Ops feature flags + billing), 3) Full Dedicated Reserved (SLA + long-term infra). Thoughts?
Anya K: I like that. Launch criteria for TieredRateLimits: implement per-org rate limits, soft overage billing, and analytics dashboard. KPIs: MRR from self-serve up 20% q/q, reduction in noisy support tickets by 30%.
Priya S: For ReservedCapacity MVP launch criteria: ability to commit a fixed monthly GPU capacity, auto-billing for committed usage, and basic enforcement with fallback policies. KPIs: convert 2 PoCs within 60 days, contract NRR +20% from those accounts.
Max C: Tech risks for TieredRateLimits: token accounting consistency across streaming calls, latency impact of rate limiter, and race conditions with cache routing. Suggest a canary with 10% of traffic.
Devon R: Sequencing trade-off: if we prioritize ReservedCapacity first, we unblock sales but delay broad monetization. If we do tiered first, we get faster ROI but might lose the big enterprise deals.
Sam L: Can we do parallel minimum efforts? A small sales-facing ReservedCapacity beta (manual ops + contract) while eng focuses on TieredRateLimits? That reduces engineering scope for reserved initial rollout.
Anya K: That seems pragmatic. Sales can accept manual activation for beta if billing and contract language are clear.
Priya S: Sales can convert manual activations into the beta — we already have 2 customers willing to pilot.
Devon R: Operational checklist for ReservedCapacity beta: manual capacity allocation UI for finance, temporary tagging in infra, billing credits/committed usage accounting. Estimate 4 weeks of effort from a small cross-functional pod.
Max C: For TieredRateLimits roadmap: Phase 1 (3 weeks) implement soft limit + telemetry, Phase 2 (4 weeks) enforce hard limits + overage billing, Phase 3 (2 weeks) analytics + billing reconciliation. Canary in Phase 1.
Sam L: Decision draft: prioritize TieredRateLimits as the engineering lead initiative, allocate a 2-squad effort. Concurrently run a lightweight ReservedCapacity beta via sales with manual ops. Revisit full ReservedCapacity engineering build next quarter.
Anya K: Decision sounds good. Document launch criteria and OKRs. I'll own the Product PRD for TieredRateLimits; Devon can own the tech spec.
Devon R: I'll put up a tech spec draft by EOD tomorrow. Will include canary plan and perf budgets.
Priya S: Sales will line up pilot customers and provide contract templates.
Sam L: Action items:
- Anya: PRD for TieredRateLimits (due 3/25)
- Devon: Tech spec + canary plan (due 3/18)
- Max: Infra risk assessment + perf budget (due 3/19)
- Priya: Confirm 2 pilot customers for ReservedCapacity beta (due 3/22)
- Sam: finalize prioritization doc and sync with GTM (due 3/21)
pm-bot: Created task list in #product-tasks
Anya K: cc @Priya S on PRD for contractual language.
Priya S: thanks — will review. :thumbsup:
Sam L: Great progress. No blockers from my side. We'll revisit RICE scoring after we collect pilot signals.
Devon R: one more note — rate-limit counters should live in the nearest region to avoid cross-region latency, added to tech spec.
Max C: Noted. Also adding quota migration strategy for existing customers to avoid surprise throttles.
Anya K: Cool. Closing this thread for now — will link PRD in the channel when ready.
